Present : Mr. Amrinder Singh Rana, Advocate, for the appellant-
applicant

. 
Mr. Raj Negi, Deputy Advocate, General for the respondent-State.
of CRMP No.3275 of 2025 Applicant-appellant is serving sentence for his conviction under Section 452, 376 and 323 IPC.
Maximum sentence has been rt imposed under Section 376 IPC, i.e. rigorous imprisonment for 10 years.

It has been submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that appellant, including his under-trial detention, has completed about 4 years 11 months' sentence, therefore, he has served almost half of the maximum sentence awarded to him and there is no likelihood of hearing the appeal in near future.
Thus, he is entitled to be enlarged on bail after suspending his sentence.

Claiming suspension of sentence on merit also, learned counsel for the appellant-applicant submits that child witness did not identify the appellant as an assailant and there was no semen detected in swab and clothes of the victim.

Learned Deputy Advocate General submits that at the time of instance, child witness was 4 years old and at the time of deposition in Court, the child was 6 years' old, and during the span of 1 years, it is quite impossible for a child of such a tender age to remember the face of the assailant and further that absence of semen, as claimed by learned counsel for the appellant-applicant, is .
no ground to disbelieve the victim, as the other material available on record, including reliable,
cogent and convincing evidence of the victim, is sufficient to prove the guilt of appellant and to convict him of for commission of offence for which he has been convicted and sentenced.
rt

The plea with respect to suspend the sentence on the ground of serving half of the awarded sentence, cannot be a ground for suspension of sentence in a case like present one, i.e. under Section 376 of the IPC, as the prescribed maximum sentence for commission of such offence is extendable to imprisonment of life and/or death penalty.
We have gone through the record and have given thoughtful consideration to the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties.

At this stage, we are of the considered opinion that no case is Deep Alias Bittu vs . State Of H.P. on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85931438/
1 made out for suspension of sentence.
Accordingly, the application is dismissed, (Vivek Singh Thakur) Judge (Romesh Verma) Judge 5th December, 2025 (Pardeep)
